value.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。
value.en: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, the imperial younger brother had just been installed as heir and tutors were chosen with care; Guang was named junior tutor with the added title grand master of splendid carriage while keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: When the emperor had returned to Luoyang, at the time the imperial younger brother was newly established; heavily selecting tutors and instruction, they made Guang Junior Tutor, added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, attendant-in-ordinary as before.

value.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。
value.en: When Emperor Huai came to the throne, Guang received the grand master of splendid carriage's gold seal and purple ribbon and was honored together with Fu Zhi.
value.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, he added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage gold seal purple ribbon, together with Fu Zhi both were seen honored and promoted.

value.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。
value.en: Soon he was named director of the masters of writing while retaining his other titles.
value.literal: Shortly he became Director of the Masters of Writing; original offices as before.

value.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。
value.en: He died of illness and was posthumously named minister of works and palace attendant.
value.literal: Because of illness he died; posthumously Minister of Works, Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。
value.en: The fall of Luoyang followed so closely that no posthumous title was ever conferred.
value.literal: It fell when capital and Luoyang overturned; in the end no posthumous name was added.

value.zh: 劉毅
value.en: Liu Yi.
value.literal: Liu Yi.

value.zh: 暾遷太原內史，趙王倫篡位，假征虜將軍，不受，與三王共舉義。
value.en: Made Taiyuan steward, he refused usurper Lun's general's baton and marched with the allied princes.
value.literal: Tun promoted to interior steward of Taiyuan—Prince Zhao Lun usurped—false general Who Subdues Caitiffs—he did not accept—joined the Three Princes in righteous rising.

value.zh: 惠帝復阼，暾為左丞，正色立朝，三台清肅。
value.en: Under restored Emperor Hui he served as left aide—grim propriety quieted the three bureaus.
value.literal: Emperor Hui restored the throne—Tun became left aide—stern dignity at court—the Three Terraces pure and solemn.

value.zh: 尋兼御史中丞，奏免尚書僕射、東安公繇及王粹、董艾等十餘人。
value.en: He soon concurrently served as palace assistant and memorialized the removal of the vice director, the Prince of Dong'an You, along with Wang Cui, Dong Ai, and more than ten others.
value.literal: Soon concurrently palace secretary—memorialized removal of vice director of the right Prince of Dong'an You—Wang Cui—Dong Ai and over ten others.

value.zh: 朝廷嘉之，遂即真。
value.en: The court approved and confirmed his posts.
value.literal: Court praised him—then confirmed full tenure.

value.zh: 遷中庶子、左衛將軍、司隸校尉，奏免武陵王澹及何綏、劉坦、溫畿、李晅等。
value.en: He rose to heir adviser—left guard colonel—metropolitan governor—and cashiered Prince Dan and several ministers.
value.literal: Promoted heir-adjunct—colonel of the left guard—metropolitan governor—memorialized removal of Prince of Wuling Dan—He Sui—Liu Tan—Wen Ji—Li Xuan and others.

value.zh: 長沙王乂討齊王冏，暾豫謀，封朱虛縣公，千八百戶。
value.en: He helped Prince Yi against Prince Jiong and earned a Zhuxu dukedom with eighteen hundred households.
value.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi attacked Prince of Qi Jiong—Tun planned beforehand—ennobled duke of Zhuxu—one thousand eight hundred households.

value.zh: 乂死，坐免。
value.en: When Yi fell Tun lost office too.
value.literal: Yi died—by association dismissed.

value.zh: 頃之，復為司隸。
value.en: Soon he returned as metropolitan governor.
value.literal: Shortly—again metropolitan governor.

value.zh: 何攀，字惠興，蜀郡郫人也。
value.en: He Pan, styled Huixing, came from Pi in Shu.
value.literal: He Pan, courtesy name Huixing, native of Pi in Shu commandery.

value.zh: 仕州為主薄。
value.en: He began as a provincial chief clerk.
value.literal: Served province as chief clerk.

value.zh: 屬刺史皇甫晏為牙門張弘所害，誣以大逆。
value.en: Inspector Huangfu Yan was murdered by Zhang Hong and smeared as a traitor.
value.literal: When Inspector Huangfu Yan was harmed by camp gate Zhang Hong—slandered with great treason.

value.zh: 時攀適丁母喪，遂詣梁州拜表，證晏不反，故晏冤理得申。
value.en: Though mourning his mother, he rode to Liangzhou and cleared Huangfu Yan’s name.
value.literal: At time Pan happened mourning mother—thereupon went to Liangzhou submitting memorial—proved Yan did not rebel—therefore Yan’s wrong managed to clear.

value.zh: 王濬為益州，辟為別駕。
value.en: Wang Jun made him provincial aide in Yi.
value.literal: Wang Jun as Yi province—summoned as aide.

value.zh: 濬謀伐吳，遣攀奉表詣台，口陳事機，詔再引見，乃令張華與攀籌量進時討之宜。
value.en: He Pan carried Wang Jun’s Wu campaign memorial to Luoyang and planned timing with Zhang Hua.
value.literal: Jun schemed attacking Wu—sent Pan bearing memorial to court—orally stated opportunity—edict twice summoned audience—ordered Zhang Hua with Pan deliberate advancing timing of attack fitness.

value.zh: 濬兼遣攀過羊祜，面陳伐吳之策。
value.en: He also briefed Yang Hu in person on the Wu invasion.
value.literal: Jun also sent Pan visit Yang Hu—face to face state attacking Wu strategies.

value.zh: 攀善於將命，帝善之，詔攀參濬軍事。
value.en: His diplomacy pleased Emperor Wu, who attached him to Wang Jun’s staff.
value.literal: Pan good at carrying orders—Emperor praised—ordered Pan assist Jun military affairs.

value.zh: 及孫皓降于濬，而王渾恚於後機，欲攻濬，攀勸濬送皓與渾，由是事解。
value.en: When Wang Hun nearly attacked Wang Jun over Sun Hao’s surrender, He Pan urged handing the captive to Hun to prevent civil bloodshed.
value.literal: When Sun Hao surrendered to Jun—yet Wang Hun angry at late timing—wished attack Jun—Pan urged Jun deliver Hao to Hun—thereby matter resolved.

value.zh: 以攀為濬輔國司馬，封關內侯。
value.en: Wang Jun named him auxiliary marshal—Marquis Within the Pass.
value.literal: Made Pan Jun aids-state marshal—enfeoffed marquis within Guan.

value.zh: 轉滎陽令，上便宜十事，甚得名稱。
value.en: As Xingyang magistrate he offered ten reform memos and won fame.
value.literal: Transferred Xingyang magistrate—submitted convenient matters ten items—greatly earned reputation.

value.zh: 除廷尉平。
value.en: He became a justice assessor.
value.literal: Appointed commandant-ping of justice.

value.zh: 時廷尉卿諸葛沖以攀蜀士，輕之，及共斷疑獄，沖始嘆服。
value.en: Zhuge Chong sneered at his Shu origins until joint trials proved his genius.
value.literal: At time commandant of justice Zhuge Chong because Pan Shu gentleman—slighted him—when together judged doubtful lawsuits—Chong then sighed admiration.

value.zh: 遷宣城太守，不行，轉散騎侍郎。
value.en: He declined Xuancheng but joined the attendant corps.
value.literal: Promoted prefect of Xuancheng—did not go—transferred regular attendant at casual riding.

value.zh: 楊駿執政，多樹親屬，大開封嘗，欲以恩澤自衛。
value.en: Regent Yang Jun stuffed offices with kin and blanketed them with patents.
value.literal: Yang Jun holding power—planted many kin—greatly opened investitures rewards—wished by grace shield self.

value.zh: 攀以為非，乃與石崇共立議奏之。
value.en: He Pan and Shi Chong jointly condemned the policy.
value.literal: Pan thought not right—thereupon with Shi Chong jointly stood memorial submitting.

value.zh: 語在崇傳。
value.en: (See the biography of Shi Chong.)
value.literal: Language is in Chong biography.

value.zh: 帝不納。
value.en: The emperor ignored them.
value.literal: Emperor did not accept.

value.zh: 以豫誅駿功，封西城侯，邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，弟逢平卿侯，兄子逵關中侯。
value.en: For merit in executing Yang Jun he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xicheng with ten thousand households and ten thousand bolts of silk; his younger brother Feng became Marquis of Pingqing and his elder brother’s son Kui Marquis Within the Pass.
value.literal: By merit participating executing Jun—enfeoffed marquis of Xicheng—ten thousand households—gift silk ten thousand bolts—younger brother Feng Pingqing marquis—elder brother’s son Kui marquis within Guan.

value.zh: 攀固讓所封戶及絹之半，餘所受者分給中外宗親，略不入己。
value.en: He refused half the silk and fiefs—sharing the rest with kin—keeping nothing.
value.literal: Pan firmly declined half of granted households and silk—remainder received distributed inside outside kin—almost none entered self.

value.zh: 遷翊軍校尉，頃之，出為東羌校尉。
value.en: He became aide colonel then Eastern Qiang colonel.
value.literal: Promoted colonel Who Aids Army—shortly—went out colonel of Eastern Qiang.

value.zh: 徵為揚州刺史，在任三年，遷大司農。
value.en: After three years as Yangzhou inspector he headed the ministry of agriculture.
value.literal: Summoned inspector of Yang province—in office three years—promoted minister of agriculture.

value.zh: 轉兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍，固讓不就。
value.en: He refused Yanzhou despite general’s banners.
value.literal: Transferred inspector of Yanzhou—added general Who Raises Hawk—firmly declined did not take.

value.zh: 太常成粲、左將軍卞粹勸攀蒞職，中詔又加切厲，攀竟稱疾不起。
value.en: Minister of Ceremonies Cheng Can and General of the Left Bian Cui urged him to take the post; an inner edict grew stern, but Pan claimed illness and would not rise.
value.literal: Minister of ceremonies Cheng Can—general left Bian Cui urged Pan take office—inner edict again stern—Pan ultimately claimed illness did not rise.

value.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，遣使召攀，更稱疾篤。
value.en: Prince Lun’s summons met another refusal—grave illness.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped—sent envoy summon Pan—again claimed grave illness.

value.zh: 倫怒，將誅之，攀不得已，扶疾赴召。
value.en: Lun threatened death—He Pan dragged himself to Luoyang.
value.literal: Lun angry—would execute—Pan had no choice—supported illness answered summons.

value.zh: 卒于洛陽，時年五十八。
value.en: He died there at fifty-eight.
value.literal: Died in Luoyang—age fifty-eight.

value.zh: 攀居心平允，蒞官整肅，愛樂人物，敦儒貴才。
value.en: Fair-minded and orderly in office, he honored scholars and talent.
value.literal: Pan dwelling mind fair—holding office stern—loved delighted men—esteemed Confucian prized talent.

value.zh: 為梁、益二州中正，引致遺滯。
value.en: As Liang-Yi rectifier he recalled unjustly blocked men.
value.literal: As grand rectifier for Liang and Yi provinces—drew in stranded men.

value.zh: 巴西陳壽、閻乂、犍為費立皆西州名士，並被鄉閭所謗，清議十餘年。
value.en: Chen Shou and western scholars suffered decade-long village boycotts.
value.literal: Baixi Chen Shou—Yan Yi—Fei Li of Qianwei—all western province famed gentlemen—together slandered by villages—pure discussion over ten years.

value.zh: 攀申明曲直，咸免冤濫。
value.en: He Pan reversed their verdicts—clearing injustice.
value.literal: Pan clarified crooked straight—all spared wrongful overflow.

value.zh: 攀雖居顯職，家甚貧素，無妾媵伎樂，惟以周窮濟乏為事。
value.en: Despite high rank he stayed poor—no concubines or musicians—only charity.
value.literal: Pan though occupied eminent office—house very poor plain—no concubines singing girls—only took relieving poverty aiding want as task.

value.zh: 子璋嗣，亦有父風。
value.en: Son He Zhang inherited his integrity.
value.literal: Son Zhang succeeded—also had father manner.

value.zh: 傅玄
value.en: Fu Xuan
value.literal: Fu Xuan.

value.zh: 楚王瑋之矯詔也，祗以聞奏稽留，免官。
value.en: When Prince Chu, Sima Wei, forged an edict, Fu Zhi was dismissed for slow reporting.
value.literal: When Prince Chu, Wei, forged the edict, Zhi because reporting was delayed was dismissed.

value.zh: 期年，遷光祿勳，復以公事免。
value.en: A year later he became grand master of splendid horses, then was removed again over a public affair.
value.literal: After a full year he was promoted grand master of splendid horses; again for public affairs he was dismissed.

value.zh: 氐人齊萬年舉兵反，以祗為行安西軍司，加常侍，率安西將軍夏侯駿討平之。
value.en: When the Di leader Qi Wannian rebelled, Fu Zhi served as acting chief of staff for the Army of the West with concurrent regular attendant, accompanying General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to crush the revolt.
value.literal: The Di man Qi Wannian raised troops in revolt; Zhi was made acting army director of Pacifying-the-West, with concurrent regular attendant, and led General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to strike and pacify him.

value.zh: 遷衛尉，以風疾遜位，就拜常侍，食卿祿秩，賜錢及床帳等。
value.en: Promoted commandant of the guards, he resigned with a palsy, was kept as regular attendant on ministerial salary, and given cash, bedding, and the like.
value.literal: He was promoted commandant of the guards, on wind illness yielded place, was then appointed regular attendant, ate ministerial salary ranks, was granted cash, bed-curtains, and so on.

value.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，門施行馬。
value.en: Soon he added the title grand counsellor of splendid horses and was allowed the mounted patrol barrier at his gate.
value.literal: Soon he was added grand counsellor of splendid horses; mounted patrol lanes were set up at his gate.

value.zh: 及趙王倫輔政，以為中書監，常侍如故，以鎮眾心。
value.en: When Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, took charge, he made Fu Zhi overseer of the secretariat, still a regular attendant, to calm public opinion.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao, Lun, directed the government, he made him overseer of the secretariat, regular attendant as before, to steady the host of hearts.

value.zh: 祗辭之以疾，倫遣御史輿祗就職。
value.en: Fu Zhi pleaded illness; Lun sent a censor with a litter to force him to his desk.
value.literal: Zhi declined on grounds of illness; Lun sent a censor to carry Zhi in a litter to take up office.

value.zh: 王戎、陳准等相與言曰：「傅公在事，吾屬無憂矣。」
value.en: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said to each other, ‘With Lord Fu at the helm we need not worry.’
value.literal: Wang Rong, Chen Zhun, and others spoke together: "With Lord Fu in charge, our sort has no worries."

value.zh: 其為物所倚信如此。
value.en: Such was the trust men placed in him.
value.literal: Thus he was trusted by others to this degree.

value.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。
value.en: When Lun seized the throne, Fu Zhi became right grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment and added palace attendant.
value.literal: When Lun usurped, he again was right grand master of splendid horses, established office, added palace attendant.

value.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。
value.en: After Emperor Hui returned, Fu Zhi asked to resign for having served the usurper; the court refused.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to the palace, Zhi because he had received illicit office asked to retire—not permitted.

value.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。
value.en: When Lun first usurped, Sun Xiu, Prince Yiyang Sima Wei, and a dozen others had drafted the abdication liturgy and text.
value.literal: At first when Lun usurped, Sun Xiu and Prince of Yiyang, Wei, and more than a dozen others pre-drafted the ceremonies and abdication texts.

value.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。
value.en: When Lun fell, Prince Qi Sima Jiong arrested Liu Dai, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others for the commandant of justice.
value.literal: When Lun fell, the prince of Qi, Jiong, seized palace attendant Liu Dai, regular attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, yellow gate gentleman Lu Ji, right aide Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.

value.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。
value.en: Because the abdication edict had issued from the secretariat, some wanted Fu Zhi punished, but a general amnesty spared him.
value.literal: Because the abdication text came from the secretariat, they again debated punishing Zhi's crime, but a general amnesty arrived and he was pardoned.

value.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。
value.en: Later it was shown the draft was not his hand, and an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.
value.literal: Later because the abdication draft in manuscript was not written by Zhi, thereupon an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.

value.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。
value.en: His son Fu Xuan married the princess of Hongnong.
value.literal: His son Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.

value.zh: 宣字世弘。
value.en: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Shihong.
value.literal: Xuan's style name was Shihong.

value.zh: 年六歲喪繼母，哭泣如成人，中表異之。
value.en: At six he lost his stepmother and wept like a grown man; kinsfolk marveled.
value.literal: At age six he lost his stepmother; he wept like an adult, and cousins marveled.

value.zh: 及長，好學，趙王倫以為相國掾、尚書郎、太子中舍人，遷司徒西曹掾。
value.en: As an adult he loved books; Prince Zhao Lun made him aide to the minister of state, secretary, heir’s gentleman, then aide in the minister of education’s western bureau.
value.literal: When grown he loved learning; Prince Zhao Lun made him aide to the minister of state, gentleman of the secretariat, palace gentleman to the heir apparent; he was promoted aide in the western bureau of the minister of education.

value.zh: 去職，累遷為秘書丞、驃騎從事中郎。
value.en: After resigning he rose to secretary’s aide and staff officer to the general who gallops to battle.
value.literal: Leaving office, by stages he was promoted secretary assistant, aide-de-camp on the staff of the general who gallops to battle.

value.zh: 惠帝至自長安，以宣為左丞，不就，遷黃門郎。
value.en: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang’an, Fu Xuan was named left aide but declined, then was made gentleman at the yellow gate.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang-an, Xuan was made left aide—he did not take office—and was promoted gentleman at the yellow gate.

value.zh: 懷帝即位，轉吏部郎，又為御史中丞。
value.en: Under Emperor Huai he became a gentleman in the ministry of personnel, then metropolitan censor again.
value.literal: When Emperor Huai mounted the throne, he was transferred to gentleman of the ministry of personnel, again became metropolitan censor.

value.zh: 卒年四十九，無子，以暢子沖為嗣。
value.en: He died at forty-nine without a son, so his brother Chang’s son Chong inherited the line.
value.literal: He died at age forty-nine, without sons; Chang's son Chong was made heir.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
value.en: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.
value.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.

value.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
value.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

value.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
value.en: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
value.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

value.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
value.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
value.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

value.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
value.en: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
value.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

value.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。
value.en: Or I will finish you.
value.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.

value.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；
value.en: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
value.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

value.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
value.en: Or I will kill her myself.
value.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

value.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
value.en: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
value.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

value.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
value.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
value.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

value.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。
value.en: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
value.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.

value.zh: 要疏如律令。」
value.en: So commands the spell.'
value.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.

value.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
value.en: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.
value.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.

value.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
value.en: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
value.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.

value.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."
value.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
value.en: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
value.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'

value.zh: 議至日西不決。
value.en: Debate stalled till dusk.
value.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

value.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
value.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
value.en: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
value.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

value.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
value.en: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
value.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

value.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
value.en: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
value.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

value.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
value.en: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
value.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

value.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
value.en: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.
value.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.

value.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。
value.en: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
value.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

value.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」
value.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."
value.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'

value.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
value.en: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
value.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

value.zh: 南風，后名；
value.en: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
value.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.

value.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
value.en: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
value.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

value.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
value.en: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
value.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.

value.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
value.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
value.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

value.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
value.en: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
value.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.

value.zh: 何不先謀之！」
value.en: Why not plot first!"
value.literal: Why not plot first!'

value.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
value.en: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
value.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.

value.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。
value.en: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
value.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

value.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
value.en: Lun was branded Jia's man.
value.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.

value.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
value.en: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
value.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.

value.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
value.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
value.en: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
value.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun assented.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
value.en: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
value.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.

value.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
value.en: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
value.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.

value.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。
value.en: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
value.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.

value.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。
value.en: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
value.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
value.en: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.
value.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

value.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
value.en: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
value.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.

value.zh: 時年二十三。
value.en: He died at twenty-three.
value.literal: He was twenty-three sui.

value.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。
value.en: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
value.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

value.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。
value.en: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
value.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

value.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
value.en: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
value.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.

value.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
value.en: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
value.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.

value.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」
value.en: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."
value.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'

value.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
value.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 臧字敬文。
value.en: Second son Zang, styled Jingwen.
value.literal: Zang, courtesy name Jingwen.

value.zh: 永康元年四月，封臨淮王。
value.en: Yongkang fourth month made Linhuai prince.
value.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.

value.zh: 己巳，詔曰：「咎征數發，奸回作變，遹既逼廢，非命而沒。
value.en: On jisi day an edict stated: "Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.
value.literal: On jisi day an edict stated: 'Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.

value.zh: 今立臧為皇太孫。
value.en: Zang named grand-heir.
value.literal: Now we establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.

value.zh: 還妃王氏以母之，稱太孫太妃。
value.en: Let Consort Wang return to act as his mother, with the title Grand Consort Dowager of the Imperial Grandson-Heir.
value.literal: Consort Wang returns to mother him—styled Grand Heir Consort Dowager.

value.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。
value.en: Staff slid from heir to grand-heir titles.
value.literal: Eastern Palace staff transferred to grand-heir posts.

value.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」
value.en: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir."
value.literal: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir.'

value.zh: 五月，倫與太孫俱之東宮，太孫自西掖門出，車服侍從皆湣懷之舊也。
value.en: May procession exited the west palace gate in Yu's old livery.
value.literal: In the fifth month Lun and the grand heir went together to the Eastern Palace; the grand heir exited the Western Side Gate—carriages, dress, and attendants all followed Minhuai's old train.

value.zh: 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉。
value.en: Luoyang wept along Bronze Camel Street.
value.literal: Reaching Bronze Camel Avenue palace women wept; attendants choked; passersby wiped tears.

value.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。
value.en: Omen mulberry mirrored heir's fall.
value.literal: The mulberry sprouted again west of the wing; when the grand heir was deposed it withered.

value.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。
value.en: Yongning coup demoted Zang—murdered at Jinyong.
value.literal: In the first month of Yongning year one Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne and demoted Zang to Prince of Puyang. Zang moved with the emperor to Jinyong and was murdered soon afterward.

value.zh: 太安初，追諡曰哀。
value.en: Tai'an era canonized Ai.
value.literal: Early in Tai'an posthumous title Ai was granted.

value.zh: 邵續
value.en: Shao Xu
value.literal: Shao Xu

value.zh: =該一名亥，本僑居京兆陰磐。
value.en: Wei Gai was also called Hai and had lived as a sojourner at Yinpan in Jingzhao.
value.literal: = Gai's other name was Hai; originally he sojourned at Yinpan in Jingzhao.

value.zh: 河間王顒之伐趙王倫，以該為將兵都尉。
value.en: When Prince Hejian marched against Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, he named Wei Gai colonel of troops.
value.literal: When Prince Hejian Sima Yong campaigned against Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he appointed Gai colonel commanding troops.

value.zh: 及劉曜攻洛陽，隨浚赴難，先領兵守金墉城，故得無他。
value.en: During Liu Yao's siege of Luoyang he rode with Wei Jun to the rescue and held the Metal Moat first, so the line held.
value.literal: When Liu Yao attacked Luoyang, he followed Jun to answer the crisis, first leading troops to defend the Metal Moat fort, therefore there was nothing else amiss.

value.zh: 曜引去，餘眾依之。
value.en: When Liu Yao drew off, the survivors rallied to him.
value.literal: Yao led his forces away; the remaining host relied on him.

value.zh: 溫嶠
value.en: Wen Jiao.
value.literal: Wen Jiao.

value.zh: 郗鑒，字道徽，高平金鄉人，漢御史大夫慮之玄孫也。
value.en: Xi Jian of Jinxiang in Gaoping—courtesy Daohui—descended from the Han imperial counselor Xi Lu.
value.literal: Xi Jian, courtesy name Daohui, was a man of Jinxiang in Gaoping, great-great-grandson of Imperial Counselor Lu of Han.

value.zh: 少孤貧，博覽經籍，躬耕隴畝，吟詠不倦。
value.en: He grew up poor and fatherless but devoured the canon, tilled his own fields, and never tired of poetry and song.
value.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he broadly read the classics, personally plowed the fields, chanting and reciting tireless.

value.zh: 以儒雅著名，不應州命。
value.en: Scholars praised his cultivation; he ignored appointments from the province.
value.literal: He was famed as a Confucian gentleman and did not answer provincial summons.

value.zh: 趙王倫辟為掾，知倫有不臣之迹，稱疾去職。
value.en: Prince Zhao Lun offered him a staff post; seeing Lun's treasonous ambitions, he resigned on grounds of illness.
value.literal: Prince Zhao Lun summoned him as aide; knowing Lun bore tokens of disloyalty, he pleaded illness and left office.

value.zh: 及倫篡，其黨皆至大官，而鑒閉門自守，不染逆節。
value.en: When Sima Lun seized the throne his followers climbed to power; Xi Jian barred his doors and kept clean of the coup.
value.literal: When Lun usurped, his clique all rose to high office, yet Jian shut his gate and kept himself pure, stained by no rebellion.

value.zh: 惠帝反正，參司空軍事，累遷太子中舍人、中書侍郎。
value.en: After Emperor Hui returned, Xi Jian joined the minister of works' staff and rose to secretary and palace attendant to the heir.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Jian joined the Minister of Works' military staff, rising through Palace Junior in the Heir's Household and Secretariat Gentleman.

value.zh: 東海王越辟為主簿，舉賢良，不行。
value.en: Sima Yue of Donghai named him chief clerk and nominated him as "worthy and good"; he declined.
value.literal: Prince Donghai Sima Yue summoned him as chief clerk; recommended as Worthy and Good—he did not take office.

value.zh: 征東大將軍苟晞檄為從事中郎。
value.en: Gou Xi, general who conquered the east, summoned him as senior clerk.
value.literal: General Who Conquers the East Gou Xi summoned him by proclamation as senior clerk.

value.zh: 晞與越方以力爭，鑒不應其召。
value.en: Gou Xi and Sima Yue were at war; Xi Jian ignored the call.
value.literal: Xi and Yue were then locked in struggle for power; Jian did not answer the summons.

value.zh: 從兄旭，晞之別駕，恐禍及己，勸之赴召，鑒終不廻，晞亦不之逼也。
value.en: His cousin Xi Xu—Gou Xi's aide—feared for himself and urged compliance; Xi Jian still refused, yet Gou Xi did not press him.
value.literal: His cousin Xu, Xi's aide, fearing disaster reaching himself, urged him to obey the summons; Jian never turned back; Xi also did not force him.

value.zh: 及京師不守，寇難鋒起，鑒遂陷於陳午賊中。
value.en: When Luoyang fell and rebels multiplied, Xi Jian fell captive to Chen Wu's gang.
value.literal: When the capital did not hold and bandit calamities sprang like spear-points, Jian thereupon fell among Chen Wu's bandit band.

value.zh: 邑人張實先求交於鑒，鑒不許。
value.en: A neighbor, Zhang Shi, had courted his friendship before; Xi Jian rejected him.
value.literal: Townsmen Zhang Shi earlier sought friendship with Jian; Jian refused.

value.zh: 至是，實於午營來省鑒疾，既而卿鑒。
value.en: Zhang Shi then visited him sick in Chen Wu's camp and presumed upon familiarity.
value.literal: Thereupon Zhang from Wu's camp came to inquire after Jian's illness; afterward he addressed Jian with undue familiarity.

value.zh: 鑒謂實曰：「相與邦壤，義不及通，何可怙亂至此邪！」
value.en: Xi Jian told him, "We were neighbors yet never exchanged courtesy—how dare you exploit rebellion to force intimacy!"
value.literal: Jian said to Shi: "We share neighboring soil yet courtesy never brought us together—how dare you rely on chaos to reach this point!

value.zh: 實大慙而退。
value.en: Zhang Shi withdrew in shame.
value.literal: Shi was greatly ashamed and withdrew.

value.zh: 午以鑒有名於世，將逼為主，鑒逃而獲免。
value.en: Chen Wu meant to make the celebrated Xi Jian his figurehead; Xi Jian escaped.
value.literal: Wu because Jian had fame in the world was about to force him to be chief; Jian fled and escaped.

value.zh: 午尋潰散，鑒得歸鄉里。
value.en: Chen Wu's band soon dissolved and Xi Jian went home.
value.literal: Wu soon scattered and collapsed; Jian was able to return to his village.

value.zh: 于時所在饑荒，州中之士素有感其恩義者，相與資贍。
value.en: Famine stalked the region, yet local scholars who remembered his decency pooled supplies for him.
value.literal: At that time famine raged everywhere; gentlemen of the province who long felt his kindness and righteousness together supplied him.

value.zh: 鑒復分所得，以賉宗族及鄉曲孤老，賴而全濟者甚多，咸相謂曰：「今天子播越，中原無伯，當歸依仁德，可以後亡。」
value.en: He shared the gifts with kinsmen and destitute neighbors. Many survived thanks to him. They said, "The emperor is a refugee and the heartland lacks a lord—only humane leadership offers shelter."
value.literal: Jian again divided what he received to relieve his lineage and village orphans and elders; many relied on him and were wholly saved—all said together: "Now the Son of Heaven wanders lost; no protector holds the central plain—we ought to attach to humane virtue and may survive afterward.

value.zh: 遂共推鑒為主，舉千餘家俱避難於魯之嶧山。
value.en: They chose Xi Jian as their leader and moved more than a thousand households to Yi Mountain in Lu for safety.
value.literal: Thereupon together they pushed Jian as chief; over a thousand households jointly fled hardship to Yi Mountain in Lu.

value.zh: 隆少為趙王倫所善，及倫專擅，召為散騎常侍。
value.en: Prince Zhao Lun favored him and named him attendant cavalry.
value.literal: Long in youth favored by Prince Zhao Lun—and when Lun monopolized power—summoned Attendant Cavalry Regular.

value.zh: 倫之篡也，以為揚州刺史。
value.en: Sima Lun made him Yangzhou inspector.
value.literal: At Lun's usurpation—appointed Inspector of Yangzhou.

value.zh: 僚屬有犯，輒依台閣峻制繩之，遠近咸怨。
value.en: He policed staff harshly—everyone resented him.
value.literal: When subordinates offended—always applied terrace severe statutes binding them—far and near alike resented.

value.zh: 尋加甯東將軍，未拜，而齊王冏檄至，中州人在軍者皆欲赴義，隆以兄子鑒為趙王掾，諸子悉在京洛，故猶豫未決。
value.en: Sima Jiong summoned loyal troops; Xi Long hesitated because kin served Sima Lun.
value.literal: Shortly additionally General Who Pacifies the East—not invested—and Prince of Qi Sima Jiong's proclamation arrived—men of Central Plain in army all wished to respond to righteousness—Long because elder brother's son Jian was Zhao prince aide—all sons in capital Luo—therefore hesitated undecided.

value.zh: 主簿趙誘、前秀才虞潭白隆曰：「當今上計，明使君自將精兵徑赴齊王；
value.en: Zhao You and Yu Tan offered three plans: "As the best plan, my lord should personally lead elite troops straight to the Prince of Qi;
value.literal: Chief Clerk Zhao You—former Cultivated Talent Yu Tan informed Long saying: "Upper plan—enlightened envoy lord personally lead crack troops straight proceed Prince of Qi;

value.zh: 中計，明使君可留督攝，速遣猛將率精兵疾赴；
value.en: Next—stay behind but rush crack troops.
value.literal: Middle plan—enlightened envoy lord may remain supervise command—swift dispatch fierce general lead crack troops urgent proceed;

value.zh: 下計，示遣兵將助，而稱背倫。」
value.en: As the worst plan, appear to dispatch generals to aid him while claiming betrayal of Lun."
value.literal: Lower plan—show dispatch troops generals aiding—yet claiming betray Lun.

value.zh: 隆素敬別駕顧彥，密與謀之。
value.en: Xi Long respected aide Gu Yan and conspired in secret.
value.literal: Long since always esteemed aide Gu Yan—secretly plotted with him.

value.zh: 彥曰：「趙誘下計，乃上策也。」
value.en: Gu Yan said Zhao You's "worst" option was actually best.
value.literal: Yan said: "Zhao You's lower plan is indeed the upper strategy.

value.zh: 西曹留承聞彥言，請見，曰：「不審明使君當今何施？」
value.en: Liu Cheng asked for an audience and said, "I do not know what course my lord intends now?"
value.literal: Western Bureau aide Liu Cheng hearing Yan's words requested audience saying: "May not ask enlightened envoy lord nowadays what policy shall apply?

value.zh: 隆曰：「我俱受二帝恩，無所偏助，惟欲守州而已。」
value.en: Xi Long said, "I alike received grace from both emperors and favor neither side—I only wish to hold the province."
value.literal: Long said: "I alike received grace from two emperors—without partial aid—I only wish to guard the province.

value.zh: 承曰：「天下者，世祖皇帝之天下也。
value.en: Liu Cheng said, "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu's succession.
value.literal: Cheng said: "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu's succession.

value.zh: 太上承代已積十年，今上取四海不平，齊王應天順時，成敗之事可見。
value.en: Emperor Hui had ruled a decade; turmoil ruled the land; Prince of Qi held Heaven's mandate—the outcome was plain.
value.literal: Grandfather succeeding substitute already piled ten years—present emperor obtaining realm unpeaceful—Prince of Qi responds Heaven obeying season—success or defeat's matter may be seen.

value.zh: 使君若顧二帝，自可不行，宜急下檄文，速遣精兵猛將。
value.en: Honor both Simas if you must—but issue orders now and rush reinforcements.
value.literal: If envoy lord attends two emperors—of himself may not march—fitting urgently issue proclamation—swiftly dispatch crack troops fierce generals.

value.zh: 若其疑惑，此州豈可得保也！」
value.en: If you hesitate, can this province be preserved!"
value.literal: If you hesitate—can this province be preserved!

value.zh: 隆無所言，而停檄六日。
value.en: Xi Long stalled six days without issuing orders.
value.literal: Long said nothing—and halted proclamation six days.

value.zh: 時甯遠將軍陳留王邃領東海都尉，鎮石頭，隆軍人西赴邃甚眾。
value.en: Prince Sima Sui of Chenliu held Stone City; Xi Long's men streamed west to join him.
value.literal: At the time General Who Pacifies the Distance Prince of Chenliu Sima Sui concurrently held Donghai commandant—garrisoned Stone Fortress—Long's troops westward to join Sui were extremely numerous.

value.zh: 隆遣從事于牛渚禁之，不得止。
value.en: Xi Long tried to block Niuzhu—they could not stem the tide.
value.literal: Long dispatched clerk at Niuzhu to forbid them—they could not stop.

value.zh: 將士憤怒，夜扶邃為主而攻之，隆父子皆死，顧彥亦被害，誣隆聚合遠近，圖為不軌。
value.en: Soldiers installed Sima Sui as leader, killed Xi Long and Gu Yan, then framed them as traitors.
value.literal: Officers and soldiers enraged—night raised Sui as chief and attacked him—Long father and son both died—Gu Yan also suffered harm—slandering Long gathered far and near plotting unorthodox rebellion.

value.zh: 隆之死也，時議莫不痛惜焉。
value.en: Every observer mourned Xi Long.
value.literal: When Long died—court debate none failed to grieve.

value.zh: 應詹字思遠，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之孫也。
value.en: Ying Zhan, whose courtesy name was Siyuan, came from Nandun in Runan; he was the grandson of Ying Qu, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant.
value.literal: Ying Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan, was a native of Nandun in Runan, and a grandson of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.

value.zh: 詹幼孤，爲祖母所養。
value.en: He lost his parents while still a boy and was brought up by his grandmother.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was raised by his grandmother.

value.zh: 年十餘歲，祖母又終，居喪毀頓，杖而後起，遂以孝聞。
value.en: After his grandmother died when he was just past ten, he mourned until his body gave way and he needed a walking stick to stand; word of his filial piety spread.
value.literal: When he was a little over ten sui, his grandmother also died; in mourning he wasted away so badly that he could rise only with a staff, and he came to be known for his filial devotion.

value.zh: 家富於財，年又稚弱，乃請族人共居，委以資產，情若至親，世以此異焉。
value.en: The family was wealthy, but he was still a child; he asked his kinsmen to share one roof with him and handed his assets into their care, treating them as his nearest kin—an act that struck people of the time as extraordinary.
value.literal: His household was rich in wealth, and he was still very young, so he invited his clansmen to live together with him, entrusting them with his property; their feelings were like those of the closest kin, and the world marveled at this on that account.

value.zh: 弱冠知名，性質素弘雅，物雖犯而弗之校，以學藝文章稱。
value.en: After his capping he won a reputation; he was steady, broad-minded, and elegant by temperament, slow to take offense when others crossed him, and admired for his scholarship, arts, and writing.
value.literal: At the capping age he was already well known; by nature he was plain, magnanimous, and refined, and though things might offend him he did not contend with them; he was esteemed for learning, craft, and literary skill.

value.zh: 司徒何劭見之曰：「君子哉若人！」
value.en: When Situ He Shao met him, he exclaimed, “Here is a true gentleman.”
value.literal: Situ He Shao, seeing him, said, “What a gentleman this man is!”

value.zh: 初辟公府，爲太子舍人。
value.en: He first received appointment from the general administration and served as Gentleman Attendant of the heir apparent.
value.literal: At first he was summoned to office from the princely administration and became Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 趙王倫以爲征東長史。
value.en: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, named him senior clerk on the staff of the eastward expedition.
value.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, appointed him Senior Clerk of the East Expedition.

value.zh: 倫誅，坐免。
value.en: After Sima Lun was put to death, Ying Zhan was stripped of office by association.
value.literal: When Lun was executed, he was implicated and dismissed.

value.zh: 成都王穎辟爲掾。
value.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, recruited him to his secretariat.
value.literal: The Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, summoned him as a retainer.

value.zh: 時驃騎從事中郎諸葛玫委長沙王乂奔鄴，盛稱乂之非。
value.en: At the time Zhuge Mei, who served as clerk on the dashing cavalry general’s staff, had left Prince Sima Yi of Changsha for Ye and was loudly blackening Yi’s name.
value.literal: At that time Zhuge Mei, Attendant Clerk on the staff of the Cavalry-in-Attendant, had abandoned Prince Sima Yi of Changsha and fled to Ye, loudly denouncing Yi’s faults.

value.zh: 玫浮躁有才辯，臨漳人士無不詣之。
value.en: Zhuge Mei was volatile yet eloquent, and everyone of standing around Linzhang beat a path to his door.
value.literal: Mei was restless and sharp-tongued; there was not a person of note in Linzhang who did not go to call on him.

value.zh: 詹與玫有舊，歎曰：「諸葛仁林何與樂毅之相詭乎！」
value.en: Zhan had known Zhuge Mei for years and sighed, “How can Zhuge Renlin diverge so wildly from the conduct of Yue Yi!”
value.literal: Zhan had old ties with Mei and sighed, saying, “How can Renlin of the Zhuge clan be so unlike the way Yue Yi comported himself!”

value.zh: 卒不見之。
value.en: He never went to see him.
value.literal: In the end he did not go to see him.

value.zh: 玫聞甚愧。
value.en: When Zhuge Mei heard, he was mortified.
value.literal: When Mei heard of this he was deeply ashamed.

value.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘，詹之祖舅也，請爲長史，謂之曰：「君器識弘深，後當代老子於荊南矣。」
value.en: Liu Hong, General Who Guards the South and Zhan’s grandfather on his mother’s side, invited him as senior clerk and told him, “Your talent and judgment run deep; in time you will succeed me in holding the Jing southlands.”
value.literal: General Who Guards the South, Liu Hong—Zhan’s maternal grandfather—asked him to serve as senior clerk and said to him, “Your capacity and insight are broad and deep; one day you will take this old man’s place south of the Jing region.”

value.zh: 仍委以軍政。
value.en: He then placed military affairs in his hands.
value.literal: Thereupon he entrusted him with military administration.

value.zh: 弘著績漢南，詹之力也。
value.en: Liu Hong’s record of achievement in the southern Han basin owed much to Ying Zhan’s exertions.
value.literal: Hong achieved merit south of the Han, and it was through Zhan’s efforts.

value.zh: 遷南平太守。
value.en: He rose to become administrator of Nanping commandery.
value.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Nanping.

value.zh: 孫惠
value.en: Sun Hui.
value.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.

value.zh: 孫惠，字德施，吳國富陽人，吳豫章太守賁曾孫也。
value.en: Sun Hui, whose courtesy name was Deshi, came from Fuyang in the old state of Wu and was a great-grandson of Ben, the Yuzhang grand administrator who had served Wu.
value.literal: Sun Hui, courtesy name Deshi, was a native of Fuyang in the state of Wu; he was a great-grandson of Ben, who had been Grand Administrator of Yuzhang under Wu.

value.zh: 父祖並仕吳。
value.en: Both his father and his grandfather had served the Wu regime.
value.literal: His father and grandfather both held office in Wu.

value.zh: 惠口訥，好學有才識，州辟不就，寓居蕭沛之間。
value.en: He was awkward in speech but a devoted student, with real ability and insight. Though the provincial authorities tried to appoint him, he stayed out of office and lived for a time between Xiao and Pei.
value.literal: Hui was slow of tongue, loved learning, and had talent and judgment; the province summoned him but he did not take office, and he lodged between Xiao and Pei.

value.zh: 永甯初，赴齊王冏義，討趙王倫，以功封晉興縣侯，辟大司馬戶曹掾，轉東曹屬。
value.en: When Yongning began, he joined Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi, in the loyalist campaign against Sima Lun, the Prince of Zhao. His service earned him the county marquisate of Jinxing, a post as clerk in the minister of war's revenue office, and then a place on the eastern staff.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era, he answered Prince of Qi Jiong's call to righteous arms and campaigned against Prince of Zhao Lun; for merit he was enfeoffed marquis of Jinxing County, appointed clerk in the Revenue Bureau of the Minister of War, then transferred to a subordinate post in the eastern bureau.

value.zh: 冏驕矜僭侈，天下失望。
value.en: Jiong grew haughty and overbearing, overstepping his rank and spending on a princely scale until the empire had lost faith in him.
value.literal: Jiong was arrogant, boastful, presumptuous, and extravagant; all under Heaven were disappointed in him.

value.zh: 惠獻言於冏，諷以五難、四不可，勸令歸籓，辭甚切至。
value.en: Sun Hui laid before him a carefully framed remonstrance—the 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities'—urging him to withdraw to his princely domain. The tone was urgent and uncompromising.
value.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities' as indirect admonition, urging him to return to his fief; the wording was extremely blunt and thorough.

value.zh: 冏不納。
value.en: Jiong refused to listen.
value.literal: Jiong did not accept it.

value.zh: 惠懼罪，辭疾去。
value.en: Fearing reprisals, Sun Hui pleaded illness and slipped away.
value.literal: Hui feared punishment, pleaded illness, and departed.

value.zh: 頃之，冏果敗。
value.en: Soon afterward Jiong fell, exactly as he had warned.
value.literal: Before long, Jiong indeed was defeated.

value.zh: 成都王穎薦惠為大將軍參軍、領奮威將軍、白沙督。
value.en: Sima Ying, the Prince of Chengdu, then recommended him as an adviser on the grand general's staff, with the concurrent titles of General Who Rouses Might and commander of the Baisha garrison.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying recommended Hui as staff adviser to the grand general, concurrently General Who Rouses Might, and commander at Baisha.

value.zh: 是時，穎將征長沙王乂，以陸機為前鋒都督。
value.en: Ying was preparing to move against Sima Yi, the Prince of Changsha, and named Lu Ji to lead the van.
value.literal: At this time Ying was about to campaign against Prince of Changsha Yi and appointed Lu Ji as commander of the vanguard.

value.zh: 惠與機同鄉里，憂其致禍，勸機讓都督于王粹。
value.en: As a townsman of Lu Ji, Sun Hui worried the appointment would destroy him and urged him to step aside in favor of Wang Cui.
value.literal: Hui was from the same home region as Ji; fearing that Ji would bring disaster on himself, he urged Ji to yield the commander's post to Wang Cui.

value.zh: 及機兄弟被戮，惠甚傷恨之。
value.en: When Lu Ji and his brothers were put to death, Sun Hui mourned them bitterly.
value.literal: When Ji and his brothers were executed, Hui deeply grieved and resented it.

value.zh: 時惠又擅殺穎牙門將梁俊，懼罪，因改姓名以遁。
value.en: He had already killed Liang Jun, one of Ying's gate generals, without orders. Dreading the consequences, he took a new identity and went into hiding.
value.literal: At that time Hui had also on his own authority killed Liang Jun, a gate-guard general under Ying; fearing punishment, he changed his name and fled into hiding.

value.zh: 初，趙王倫篡位，三王起義，制《己亥格》，其後論功雖小，亦皆依用。
value.en: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and afterward even small merit awards all continued to use that code.
value.literal: At first, when Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, the three princes raised the righteous army and established the 《Yihai Precedent》; afterward, in discussing merit, even small cases all relied on it.

value.zh: 頵意謂不宜以為常式，駁之曰：「聖王懸爵賞功，制罰糾違，斯道苟明，人赴水火。
value.en: Chen Yun argued it must not become permanent law: 'Sage kings reward merit and punish crime—make that clear and men will walk through fire for you.
value.literal: Yun held that it should not be taken as a constant model and refuted it, saying, "The sage kings suspend ranks to reward merit and institute punishments to correct transgressions—if this way is clear, men will throw themselves into water and fire.

value.zh: 且名器之實，不可妄假，非才謂之致寇，寵厚戒在斯亡。
value.en: Titles are not party favors; calling fools worthy invites rebellion; showering empty rank is how dynasties die.
value.literal: Moreover the substance of names and vessels must not be rashly lent; calling the unworthy talented is what brings bandits; the warning that thick favor lies in this perishing.

value.zh: 昔孫秀口唱篡逆，手弄天機，惠皇失禦，九服無戴。
value.en: Sun Xiu preached treason and toyed with the edict; Emperor Hui lost control, and no one in the nine circuits wore the cap straight.
value.literal: Formerly Sun Xiu mouthed usurpation and treason and with his hands played with Heaven's mechanism; Emperor Hui lost the reins, and within the nine domains there was none who wore the cap of loyalty.

value.zh: 三王建議，席捲四海，合起義之眾，結天下之心，故設《己亥義格》以權濟難。
value.en: The three princes swept the realm, welded the loyal armies, and issued the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 as a temporary wartime ladder.
value.literal: The three princes set up the plan; they rolled up the four seas; they combined the hosts of the righteous uprising and bound the mind of all under Heaven; therefore they established the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 to weigh and relieve the hardship.

value.zh: 此自一切之法，非常倫之格也。
value.en: That was an emergency rulebook, not a peacetime statute.
value.literal: This was itself an expedient one-time law, not a standard for ordinary categories.

value.zh: 其起義以來，依格雜猥，遭人為侯，或加兵伍，或出皁僕，金紫佩士卒之身，符策委庸隸之門，使天官降辱，王爵黷賤，非所以正皇綱重名器之謂也。
value.en: Since then the code has handed marquisates to pull, put silks on privates, and stuffed tally books into lackeys' sleeves—that is not how you mend the net of state or honor a title.
value.literal: From the uprising onward, according to the precedent it has been mixed and base: persons have been made marquis by pull, some added to the ranks of soldiers, some issued from black servants; gold and purple hang on troopers' persons; tallies and registers lie in menial slaves' gates—this is not what is called rectifying the imperial net and valuing names and vessels.

value.zh: 請自今以後宜停之。」
value.en: Abolish it from this day forward.'
value.literal: I ask that from now on it be stopped."

value.zh: 頵以孤寒，數有奏議，朝士多惡之，出除譙郡太守。
value.en: Chen Yun had no faction and a cold pedigree; his blunt papers earned him enemies, and the court parked him as grand administrator of Qiao.
value.literal: Because Yun was isolated and of cold background, he repeatedly had memorials and proposals; court gentlemen mostly hated him, and he was sent out as grand administrator of Qiao commandery.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 喬智明，字元達，鮮卑前部人也。
value.en: Qiao Zhiming (courtesy Yuanda) belonged to the forward wing of the Xianbei confederation.
value.literal: Qiao Zhiming, courtesy name Yuanda, was a man of the forward division of the Xianbei.

value.zh: 少喪二親，哀毀過禮，長而以德行著稱。
value.en: Orphaned young, he mourned beyond ritual and matured renowned for character.
value.literal: In youth he lost both parents; his grief exceeded ritual propriety; grown, he was famed for virtuous conduct.

value.zh: 成都王穎辟為輔國將軍。
value.en: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying appointed him General Who Supports the State.
value.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as General Who Supports the State.

value.zh: 穎之敗趙王倫也，表智明為殄寇將軍、隆慮、共二縣令。
value.en: After defeating Prince Zhao Sima Lun, Sima Ying named him General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong.
value.literal: When Ying defeated Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he memorialized Zhiming as General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong counties.

value.zh: 二縣愛之，號為「神君」。
value.en: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."
value.literal: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."

value.zh: 部人張兌為父報仇，母老單身，有妻無子，智明湣之，停其獄。
value.en: Commoner Zhang Dui killed for vengeance; his mother lived alone and he lacked an heir; Qiao Zhiming stayed judgment out of mercy.
value.literal: A local man Zhang Dui avenged his father; his mother was old and lived alone; he had a wife but no son; Zhiming pitied him and stayed the case.

value.zh: 歲餘，令兌將妻入獄，兼陰縱之。
value.en: After a year he let Zhang bring his wife into custody and quietly allowed intimacy.
value.literal: After more than a year he ordered Dui to bring his wife into jail and secretly allowed conjugal visits.

value.zh: 人有勸兌逃者，兌曰：「有君如此，吾何忍累之！
value.en: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!
value.literal: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!

value.zh: 縱吾得免，作何面目視息世間！」
value.en: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"
value.literal: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"

value.zh: 於獄產一男。
value.en: His wife delivered a son in prison.
value.literal: In the jail his wife bore a boy.

value.zh: 會赦，得免。
value.en: An amnesty freed him.
value.literal: An amnesty arrived and he obtained release.

value.zh: 其仁感如是。
value.en: Such was the power of his humane rule.
value.literal: His humane kindness moved people thus.

value.zh: 惠帝之伐鄴也，穎以智明為折沖將軍、參丞相前鋒軍事。
value.en: During Emperor Hui's expedition against Ye, Sima Ying made him General Who Charges the Enemy on the vanguard staff.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Ye, Ying appointed Zhiming General Who Charges the Enemy and adjutant on the prime minister's vanguard staff.

value.zh: 智明勸穎奉迎乘輿，穎大怒曰：「卿名曉事，投身事孤。
value.en: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.
value.literal: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.

value.zh: 主上為群小所逼，將加非罪於孤，卿奈何欲使孤束手就刑邪！
value.en: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!
value.literal: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!

value.zh: 共事之義，正若此乎？」
value.en: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"
value.literal: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"

value.zh: 智明乃止。
value.en: Qiao Zhiming fell silent.
value.literal: Zhiming thereupon desisted.

value.zh: 尋屬永嘉之亂，仕于劉曜。
value.en: When Yongjia chaos erupted he entered Liu Yao's Han-Zhao regime.
value.literal: Soon the Yongjia turmoil came; he served Liu Yao.

value.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
value.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
value.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

value.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
value.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
value.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.

value.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
value.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
value.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

value.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
value.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
value.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

value.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
value.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
value.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

value.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
value.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
value.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

value.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
value.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
value.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

value.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
value.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
value.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

value.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
value.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
value.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

value.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
value.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
value.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

value.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
value.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
value.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

value.zh: 郭琦，字公偉，太原晉陽人也。
value.en: Guo Qi, courtesy name Gongwei, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.
value.literal: Guo Qi, styled Gongwei, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

value.zh: 少方直，有雅量，博學，善五行，作《天文志》、《五行傳》，注《穀梁》、《京氏易》百卷。
value.en: Young, upright, and learned in astrology, he wrote treatises on heaven, the five phases, and a hundred fascicles on the Guliang and Jing Changes.
value.literal: In youth he was square and straight, had a refined capacity, was broadly learned, skilled in the five phases, and composed the Monograph on Heaven, the Traditions of the Five Phases, and a hundred rolls of commentary on the Guliang Annals and the Jing family Changes.

value.zh: 鄉人王遊等皆就琦學。
value.en: Townsmen such as Wang You studied at his feet.
value.literal: His townsman Wang You and others all came to Qi to study.

value.zh: 武帝欲以琦為佐著作郎，問琦族人尚書郭彰。
value.en: Emperor Wu meant to name him assistant editor and asked his kinsman Guo Zhang.
value.literal: Emperor Wu wished to make Qi assistant editorialist and asked Qi's clansman Minister Guo Zhang.

value.zh: 彰素疾琦，答云：「不識」。
value.en: Zhang hated him and said flatly, 'I never heard of him.'
value.literal: Zhang by nature detested Qi and answered, "I do not know him."

value.zh: 帝曰：「若如卿言，烏丸家兒能事卿，即堪為郎矣。」
value.en: The emperor retorted, 'If a Wuhuan stable-boy is good enough for you, he is good enough for my editorial office.'
value.literal: The emperor said, "If it is as you say, then a Wuhuan household lad who can serve you would be fit to be a gentleman!"

value.zh: 遂決意用之。
value.en: So the emperor appointed Qi anyway.
value.literal: Thereupon he resolved to employ him.

value.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，又欲用琦，琦曰：「我已為武帝吏，不容復為今世吏。」
value.en: When Sima Lun seized the throne and offered a post, Qi answered, "I served Emperor Wu; I will not serve your court."
value.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun usurped the throne, he again wished to use Qi; Qi said, "I have already been an official to Emperor Wu; I cannot again be an official to today's world."

value.zh: 終身處於家。
value.en: He stayed home for life.
value.literal: To the end of his life he remained at home.

value.zh: 慕容德
value.en: Murong De.
value.literal: Murong De.

value.zh: 至是，慕容寶自龍城南奔至黎陽，遣其中黃門令趙思召慕容鍾來迎。
value.en: Murong Bao then fled south from Longcheng to Liyang and dispatched Zhao Si, his central palace gate director, to call Murong Zhong to escort him.
value.literal: At this point Murong Bao fled south from Longcheng to Liyang and sent his central yellow-gate director Zhao Si to summon Murong Zhong to come welcome him.

value.zh: 鍾本首議勸德稱尊號，聞而惡之，執思付獄，馳使白狀。
value.en: Murong Zhong, who had first urged Murong De to take the throne, took offense, jailed Zhao Si, and sent a courier to inform Murong De.
value.literal: Murong Zhong had originally been first to urge Murong De to assume the exalted title, and when he heard this he hated it, seized Zhao Si and handed him to prison, and galloped a messenger to report the situation.

value.zh: 德謂其下曰：「卿等前以社稷大計，勸吾攝政。
value.en: Murong De told his subordinates: “Earlier, for the great plan of the altars of state, you urged me to take the regency.
value.literal: Murong De told his subordinates: “Earlier, for the great plan of the altars of state, you urged me to take the regency.

value.zh: 吾亦以嗣帝奔亡，人神曠主，故權順群議，以系眾望。
value.en: I also, because the heir emperor had fled and men and spirits lacked a lord, temporarily followed the counsel of the crowd in order to hold the hopes of the multitude.
value.literal: I also, because the heir emperor had fled and men and spirits lacked a lord, temporarily followed the counsel of the crowd in order to hold the hopes of the multitude.

value.zh: 今天方悔禍，嗣帝得還，吾將具駕奉迎，謝罪行闕，然後角巾私第，卿等以為何如？」
value.en: Now Heaven is beginning to repent of the calamity, and the heir emperor may return. I will prepare my carriage to welcome him, apologize for my crimes at the traveling palace, and afterward retire in a scholar’s headcloth to a private house. What do you think?”
value.literal: Now Heaven is beginning to repent of the calamity, and the heir emperor may return. I will prepare my carriage to welcome him, apologize for my crimes at the traveling palace, and afterward retire in a scholar’s headcloth to a private house. What do you think?”

value.zh: 其黃門侍郎張華進曰：「夫爭奪之世，非雄才不振；
value.en: His Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zhang Hua stepped forward and said: “In an age of struggle, only heroic talent can rouse the realm;
value.literal: His Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zhang Hua stepped forward and said: “In an age of struggle, only heroic talent can rouse the realm;

value.zh: 從橫之時，豈懦夫能濟！
value.en: in a time of maneuvering, how could a coward accomplish rescue?
value.literal: in a time of maneuvering, how could a coward accomplish rescue?

value.zh: 陛下若蹈匹婦之仁，舍天授之業，威權一去，則身首不保，何退讓之有乎！」
value.en: If Your Majesty treads the kindness of a common woman, abandons the enterprise bestowed by Heaven, and lets authority and awe depart, then body and head will not be preserved. What room is there for yielding?”
value.literal: If Your Majesty treads the kindness of a common woman, abandons the enterprise bestowed by Heaven, and lets authority and awe depart, then body and head will not be preserved. What room is there for yielding?”

value.zh: 德曰：「吾以古人逆取順守，其道未足，所以中路徘徊，悵然未決耳。」
value.en: Murong De said: “I considered how the ancients seized power against the current and guarded it in accord with right, but my way is not yet sufficient; that is why I halted midway in hesitation, despondent and undecided.”
value.literal: Murong De said: “I considered how the ancients seized power against the current and guarded it in accord with right, but my way is not yet sufficient; that is why I halted midway in hesitation, despondent and undecided.”

value.zh: 慕輿護請馳問寶虛實，德流涕而遣之。
value.en: Yu Hu volunteered to ride north and learn Murong Bao's true situation; Murong De sent him off in tears.
value.literal: Yu Hu requested to gallop and inquire into Murong Bao's truth and falsehood, and Murong De wept as he sent him.

value.zh: 乃率壯士數百，隨思而北，因謀殺寶。
value.en: He led hundreds of picked men north with Zhao Si plotting to murder Murong Bao.
value.literal: Yu Hu then led several hundred stalwarts and followed Zhao Si northward and plotted to kill Murong Bao.

value.zh: 初，寶遣思之後，知德攝位，懼而北奔。
value.en: After dispatching Zhao Si, Murong Bao had learned of Murong De's assumption of power and fled north in fear.
value.literal: Earlier, after Murong Bao had sent Zhao Si, he learned that Murong De had taken the position and was afraid and fled north.

value.zh: 護至無所見，執思而還。
value.en: Yu Hu found no sign of Murong Bao, seized Zhao Si, and came back.
value.literal: When Yu Hu arrived he saw nothing, seized Zhao Si, and returned.

value.zh: 德以思閑習典故，將任之。
value.en: Murong De intended to employ Zhao Si for his knowledge of court precedent.
value.literal: Murong De, because Zhao Si was versed in precedents and stories, was about to employ him.

value.zh: 思曰：「昔關羽見重曹公，猶不忘先主之恩。
value.en: Zhao Si said: “Formerly Guan Yu was esteemed by Cao Cao, yet still did not forget his former lord’s kindness.
value.literal: Zhao Si said: “Formerly Guan Yu was esteemed by Cao Cao, yet still did not forget his former lord’s kindness.

value.zh: 思雖刑餘賤隸，荷國寵靈，犬馬有心，而況人乎！
value.en: Though I, Si, am a mutilated and base slave, I have received the state’s favor. Dogs and horses have hearts; how much more men!
value.literal: Though I, Si, am a mutilated and base slave, I have received the state’s favor. Dogs and horses have hearts; how much more men!

value.zh: 乞還就上，以明微節。」
value.en: I beg to return to my sovereign in order to make clear my slight integrity.”
value.literal: I beg to return to my sovereign in order to make clear my slight integrity.”

value.zh: 德固留之，思怒曰：「周室衰微，晉、鄭夾輔；
value.en: Murong De firmly detained him. Si grew angry and said: “When the Zhou house declined, Jin and Zheng supported it on either side;
value.literal: Murong De firmly detained him. Si grew angry and said: “When the Zhou house declined, Jin and Zheng supported it on either side;

value.zh: 漢有七國之難，實賴梁王。
value.en: when Han suffered the trouble of the seven states, it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.
value.literal: when Han suffered the trouble of the seven states, it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.

value.zh: 殿下親則叔父，位則上臺，不能率先群後以匡王室，而幸根本之傾為趙倫之事。
value.en: Your Highness, in kinship, is the emperor’s uncle, and in rank you stand among the highest ministers, yet you cannot lead the lords in aiding the royal house, but instead rejoice in the collapse of the root and foundation and act like Zhao Lun.
value.literal: Your Highness, in kinship, is the emperor’s uncle, and in rank you stand among the highest ministers, yet you cannot lead the lords in aiding the royal house, but instead rejoice in the collapse of the root and foundation and act like Zhao Lun.

value.zh: 思雖無申胥哭秦之效，猶慕君賓不生莽世。」
value.en: Though I, Si, lack Shen Baoxu’s effect of weeping at Qin, I still admire Junbin for refusing to live in Wang Mang’s age.”
value.literal: Though I, Si, lack Shen Baoxu’s effect of weeping at Qin, I still admire Junbin for refusing to live in Wang Mang’s age.”

value.zh: 德怒，斬之。
value.en: Murong De flew into a rage and had him executed.
value.literal: De was angry and beheaded him.

value.zh: 齊王冏既誅趙倫，因留輔政，坐拜百官，符敕臺府，淫醟專驕，不一朝覲。
value.en: After Sima Jiong of Qi had killed Zhao Lun he stayed on as regent, accepted officials' bows while seated, issued Secretariat orders at will, and grew drunken, arrogant, and aloof—never attending court.
value.literal: After the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, had executed Zhao Lun, he remained to assist in government, sat to receive the obeisance of all officials, issued orders in the name of the Secretariat, and was dissolute, arrogant, and exclusive—never once attending court audience.

value.zh: 此狂恣不肅之容也。
value.en: This was the deportment of reckless insolence without respect.
value.literal: This was the bearing of mad presumption without reverence.

value.zh: 天下莫不高其功，而慮其亡也。
value.en: The empire applauded his success yet dreaded his fall.
value.literal: Throughout the realm none failed to praise his achievement, yet all feared his ruin.

value.zh: 冏終弗改，遂至夷滅。
value.en: Jiong never reformed and was destroyed in the end.
value.literal: Jiong in the end did not change and proceeded to extermination.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 太子既廢，眾情憤怒。
value.en: Once the heir apparent was deposed, public anger boiled over.
value.literal: Once the Heir Apparent was deposed, public sentiment was furious.

value.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
value.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
value.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 以張華、裴頠安常保位，難與行權，右軍將軍趙王倫執兵柄，性貪冒，可假以濟事。
value.en: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei too cautious to act, while Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, held the armies and was greedy—he could be used.
