value.literal: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei content to preserve their posts and hard to move to action, while the General of the Right Army the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun held military power and was greedy—he could be borrowed to accomplish the affair.

value.zh: 乃說孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共誣廢太子。
value.en: They told Sun Xiu: "The empress is vicious and lawless. With Jia Mi she framed and deposed the heir apparent.
value.literal: They thereupon said to Sun Xiu: "The central palace is fierce, jealous, and without the Way, and together with Jia Mi and others falsely deposed the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事，而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及，何不先謀之乎！」
value.en: The realm lacks a legitimate heir and the altars are endangered. Great ministers will act, yet you serve the empress and are close to the Jia and Guo clans. When the heir apparent fell, men said you knew beforehand. When trouble erupts you will not escape—why not strike first?"
value.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir and the altars are in peril; the great ministers will raise a great affair, yet you by name attend the central palace and are intimate with the Jia and Guo—when the Heir Apparent was deposed all said you foreknew it. Once trouble rises disaster must reach you—why not plot first!"

value.zh: 秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉，遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡等，使為內應。
value.en: Xiu agreed and told Lun, who accepted and enlisted Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng as inside agents.
value.literal: Xiu promised and spoke to Lun; Lun accepted, and reported to the clerks Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng among the communications staff to serve as inside agents.

value.zh: 事將起，孫秀言於倫曰：「太子聰明剛猛，若還東宮，必不受制於人。
value.en: Before the coup Sun Xiu told Lun: "The heir apparent is clever and fierce. Restored to the Eastern Palace he will not submit to anyone.
value.literal: As the affair was about to begin, Sun Xiu said to Lun: "The Heir Apparent is intelligent, stern, and fierce; if restored to the Eastern Palace he will surely not be controlled by others.

value.zh: 明公素黨於賈后，道路皆知之，今雖建大功於太子，太子謂公特逼於百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳，雖含忍宿忿，必不能深德明公，若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: You have always sided with the empress—everyone knows it. Even if you now save him, he will think you acted only under public pressure and may turn on you to clear himself. Old grudges will not become deep gratitude; the slightest fault could still cost your life.
value.literal: Your Excellency has always been of the empress's party—the roads all know it. Though you now perform a great service for the Heir Apparent, he will say you acted only under the people's pressure and may turn to escape guilt; though he swallow old resentment he cannot deeply reward you, and if there be a flaw you still cannot escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延緩期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，豈徒免禍而已，乃更可以得志！」
value.en: Delay instead. The empress will kill him. Then depose her and avenge him—not merely escaping harm but winning your ambition!"
value.literal: Better to delay and wait: the empress will surely harm the Heir Apparent; then depose the empress and avenge the Heir Apparent—not only escaping disaster but gaining your ambition!"

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun agreed.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使人行反間，言殿中人欲廢皇后，迎太子。
value.en: Xiu spread disinformation that palace insiders meant to depose the empress and restore the heir apparent.
value.literal: Xiu therefore sent men to spread counter-intelligence, saying those in the palace wished to depose the empress and welcome the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 賈后數遣宮婢微服於民間聽察，聞之甚懼。
value.en: The empress often sent maids in disguise to listen among the people and was terrified.
value.literal: Empress Jia often sent palace maids in plain dress among the people to listen; hearing this she was greatly afraid.

value.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早除太子，以絕眾望。
value.en: Lun and Xiu urged Mi and others to kill the heir apparent at once and end public hope.
value.literal: Lun and Xiu therefore urged Mi and the rest to eliminate the Heir Apparent early and cut off public hope.

value.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。
value.en: On guimao the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
value.literal: On the day guimao Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

value.zh: 矯詔使黃門孫慮至許昌毒太子。
value.en: A forged edict sent Sun Lv of the Yellow Gate to Xuchang to poison the heir apparent.
value.literal: A forged edict sent the Yellow Gate Sun Lv to Xuchang to poison the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 太子自廢黜，恐被毒，常自煮食於前；
value.en: Since his deposition he feared poison and often cooked for himself;
value.literal: Since his deposition the Heir Apparent feared poison and often cooked his own food beforehand;

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。
value.en: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.
value.literal: Lv reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen then moved the Heir Apparent to a small compound and cut off his food, yet palace women still secretly passed food over the wall.

value.zh: 慮逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，慮以藥杵椎殺之。
value.en: Lv forced the drug on him; he refused; Lv beat him to death with the pestle.
value.literal: Lv forced the Heir Apparent to take the drug; he refused; Lv killed him with the drug pestle.

value.zh: 有司請以庶人禮葬，賈后表請以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: Officials requested commoner burial; the empress asked for princely rites as for the Prince of Guangling.
value.literal: The authorities requested burial with commoner rites; the empress memorialized for burial with the rites of a Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。
value.en: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.
value.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.

value.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
value.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
value.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

value.zh: 華拒之。
value.en: Hua refused.
value.literal: Hua refused.

value.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
value.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
value.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

value.zh: 不顧而出。
value.en: He strode out without a backward glance.
value.literal: He left without looking back.

value.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」
value.en: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."
value.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."

value.zh: 眾皆從之。
value.en: All obeyed.
value.literal: All obeyed.

value.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。
value.en: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.
value.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.

value.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」
value.en: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
value.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

value.zh: 就斬之。
value.en: He was beheaded at once.
value.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.

value.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」
value.en: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"
value.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
value.en: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."
value.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."

value.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」
value.en: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
value.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

value.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」
value.en: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."
value.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."

value.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
value.en: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"
value.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
value.en: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
value.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

value.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」
value.en: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"
value.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"

value.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。
value.en: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.
value.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.

value.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。
value.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
value.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

value.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。
value.en: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.
value.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.

value.zh: 倫陰與秀謀篡位，欲先除朝望，且報宿怨，乃執張華、裴頠、解系、解結等於殿前。
value.en: Lun secretly plotted usurpation with Xiu, first removing leading ministers and settling old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others in the hall.
value.literal: Lun secretly plotted with Xiu to usurp the throne, wishing first to remove men of court esteem and also settle old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others before the hall.

value.zh: 華謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣邪？」
value.en: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you mean to kill loyal ministers?"
value.literal: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish to harm loyal ministers?"

value.zh: 林稱詔詰之曰：「卿為宰相，太子之廢，不能死節，何也？」
value.en: Lin, citing the edict, demanded: "As chief minister, when the heir apparent was deposed why did you not die for principle?"
value.literal: Lin, claiming the edict, interrogated him: "You were chief minister; when the Heir Apparent was deposed you could not die for principle—why?"

value.zh: 華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，可覆按也。」
value.en: Hua said: "My remonstrance at the Shiqian deliberation is on record and may be reviewed."
value.literal: Hua said: "On the deliberation at Shiqian my remonstrance is fully recorded and may be reviewed."

value.zh: 林曰：「諫而不從，何不去位？」
value.en: Lin said: "If remonstrance failed, why not resign?"
value.literal: Lin said: "If you remonstrated and were not obeyed, why not leave office?"

value.zh: 華無以對。
value.en: Hua had no answer.
value.literal: Hua had no reply.

value.zh: 遂皆斬之，仍夷三族。
value.en: All were beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.
value.literal: They were all beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

value.zh: 解結女適裴氏，明日當嫁而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何以活為！」
value.en: Xie Jie's daughter was to marry into the Pei clan next day when disaster struck; the Peis wished to save her; she said: "With my house destroyed, how can I live!"
value.literal: Xie Jie's daughter was betrothed to the Pei clan; the wedding was due the next day when disaster struck; the Pei wished to claim her alive; the girl said: "With my house thus, how can I live!"

value.zh: 亦坐死。
value.en: She died as well.
value.literal: She too died for it.

value.zh: 朝廷由是議革舊制，女不從死。
value.en: The court then debated abolishing the old rule that wives and daughters die with the clan.
value.literal: The court thereupon debated abolishing the old rule that daughters follow their kin to death.

value.zh: 甲午，倫坐端門，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人於金墉；
value.en: On jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed empress to Jinyong;
value.literal: On the day jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent the Masters of Writing He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed Jia commoner to Jinyong;

value.zh: 誅劉振、董猛、孫慮、程據等；
value.en: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;
value.literal: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;

value.zh: 司徒王戎及內外官坐張、裴親黨黜免者甚眾。
value.en: Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and many inner and outer officials were dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei.
value.literal: the Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and inner and outer officials dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei were very numerous.

value.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」
value.en: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
value.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"

value.zh: 於是趙王倫稱詔赦天下，自為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、相國、侍中，一依宣、文輔魏故事。
value.en: Lun proclaimed amnesty, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of the Sima regents of Wei.
value.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Zhao Lun proclaimed an edict amnestying the realm, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of Xuan and Wen in assisting Wei.

value.zh: 置府兵萬人，以其世子散騎常侍荂領冗從僕射，子馥為前將軍，封濟陽王；
value.en: He stationed ten thousand household troops; his heir Fu, Regular Attendant, held redundant Follower posts; son Fu was Forward General, Prince of Jiyang;
value.literal: He stationed ten thousand troops at his headquarters; his heir, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment Fu, held redundant Followers as Vice-Director; his son Fu was Forward General and Prince of Jiyang;

value.zh: 虔為黃門朗，封汝陰王；
value.en: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;
value.literal: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;

value.zh: 詡為散騎侍郎，封霸城侯。
value.en: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.
value.literal: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.

value.zh: 孫秀等皆封大郡，並據兵權，文武官封侯者數千人，百官總己以聽於倫。
value.en: Sun Xiu and others received great fiefs and military power; thousands of officials were enfeoffed; all offices reported to Lun.
value.literal: Sun Xiu and the rest were all enfeoffed in great commanderies and held military power; civil and military officials enfeoffed as marquis numbered in the thousands; the hundred offices all reported to Lun.

value.zh: 倫素庸愚，復受制於孫秀。
value.en: Lun was mediocre and foolish and controlled by Sun Xiu.
value.literal: Lun was by nature mediocre and foolish and again controlled by Sun Xiu.

value.zh: 秀為中書令，威權振朝廷，天下皆事秀而無求於倫。
value.en: Xiu became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.
value.literal: Xiu was Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.

value.zh: 相國倫欲收入望，選用海內名德之士，以前平陽太守李重、滎陽太守荀組為左、右長史，東平王堪、沛國劉謨為左、右司馬，尚書郎陽平束皙為記室，淮南王文學荀嵩、殿中郎陸機為參軍。
value.en: Lun sought esteem and recruited renowned men: Li Chong and Xun Zu as chief clerks; Kan, Prince of Dongping, and Liu Mo as majors; Shuxi as recorder; Xun Song and Lu Ji on staff.
value.literal: Chancellor Lun wished to win esteem and selected men of virtue throughout the realm: the former Administrator of Pingyang Li Chong and Administrator of Xingyang Xun Zu as Left and Right Chief Clerks; the Prince of Dongping Kan and Liu Mo of Peiguo as Left and Right Majors; Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Shuxi of Yangping as Recorder; the Literary Scholar of Huainan Xun Song and Palace Gentleman Lu Ji as Staff.

value.zh: 組，勖之子；
value.en: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;
value.literal: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;

value.zh: 嵩，彧之玄孫也。
value.en: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.
value.literal: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.

value.zh: 李重知倫有異志，辭疾不就，倫逼之不已，憂憤成疾，扶曳受拜，數日而卒。
value.en: Li Chong saw Lun's rebellious intent, pleaded illness, was forced to accept office, and died within days of grief.
value.literal: Li Chong knew Lun harbored rebellious intent, declined illness and would not come; Lun pressed him without cease; he fell ill from grief and anger, was carried in to accept appointment, and died within days.

value.zh: 太子遹之廢也，將立淮南王允為太弟，議者不合。
value.en: When Yu was deposed they considered making Yun, Prince of Huainan, heir younger brother; deliberators disagreed.
value.literal: When the Heir Apparent Yu was deposed, they were about to establish the Prince of Huainan Yun as heir younger brother; deliberators did not agree.

value.zh: 會趙王倫廢賈后，乃以允為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，領中護軍。
value.en: When Lun deposed the empress, Yun was made General of Agile Cavalry with Three Excellencies privilege and Central Protector.
value.literal: When the Prince of Zhao Lun deposed Empress Jia, Yun was made General of Agile Cavalry with privilege as the Three Excellencies and Commander of the Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 己亥，相國倫矯詔遣尚書劉弘繼金屑酒，賜賈后死於金墉城。
value.en: On jihai Lun forged an edict sending Liu Hong with golden crumbs wine to kill the deposed empress at Jinyong.
value.literal: On the day jihai Chancellor Lun forged an edict sending the Masters of Writing Liu Hong with golden crumbs wine to grant the deposed Jia empress death at Jinyong.

value.zh: 五月，己巳，詔立臨淮王臧為皇太孫，還妃王氏以母之；
value.en: In the fifth month, on jisi, Zang, Prince of Linhuai, was made Imperial Grandson and Lady Wang restored as his mother;
value.literal: In the fifth month, on the day jisi, an edict established the Prince of Linhuai Zang as Imperial Grandson and returned Consort Lady Wang as his mother;

value.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬，相國倫行太孫太傅。
value.en: Eastern Palace staff became the Grandson's staff, and Lun acted as Grand Tutor.
value.literal: Eastern Palace officials became Grandson's officials, and Chancellor Lun acted as Grandson's Grand Tutor.

value.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。
value.en: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.
value.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.

value.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；
value.en: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;
value.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;

value.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。
value.en: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.
value.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.

value.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。
value.en: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.
value.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.

value.zh: 允稱疾不拜。
value.en: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.
value.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.

value.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。
value.en: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.
value.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.

value.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。
value.en: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.
value.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.

value.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」
value.en: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
value.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

value.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」
value.en: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."
value.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."

value.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。
value.en: Many rallied to him.
value.literal: At this very many came over to him.

value.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。
value.en: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.
value.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.

value.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。
value.en: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.
value.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.

value.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。
value.en: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.
value.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.

value.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。
value.en: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.
value.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.

value.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。
value.en: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.
value.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.

value.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」
value.en: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
value.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."

value.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。
value.en: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.
value.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.

value.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」
value.en: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."
value.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."

value.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。
value.en: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
value.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

value.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；
value.en: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yin dismounted to receive the edict;
value.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yin dismounted to receive the edict;

value.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。
value.en: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.
value.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.

value.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
value.en: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
value.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

value.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。
value.en: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, whom he had often flogged.
value.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.

value.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。
value.en: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.
value.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.

value.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。
value.en: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.
value.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.

value.zh: 崇歎曰：「奴輩利吾財爾！」
value.en: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"
value.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"

value.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」
value.en: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"
value.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"

value.zh: 崇不能答。
value.en: Chong had no answer.
value.literal: Chong could not answer.

value.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」
value.en: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"
value.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"

value.zh: 及敗，岳謝母曰：「負阿母。」
value.en: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
value.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

value.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。
value.en: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.
value.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.

value.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。
value.en: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, younger brother of Yun's mother, intending to kill him.
value.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, younger brother of the Prince of Huainan's mother, intending to kill him.

value.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。
value.en: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.
value.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.

value.zh: 孫秀議加相國倫九錫，百官莫敢異議。
value.en: Xiu proposed granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; no official dared object.
value.literal: Sun Xiu proposed granting Chancellor Lun the Nine Bestowals; the hundred officials dared not dissent.

value.zh: 吏部尚書劉頌曰：「昔漢之錫魏，魏之錫晉，皆一時之用，非可通行。
value.en: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "When Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin, those were expedients of the moment, not universal precedent.
value.literal: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "In the past Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin—all were expedients of the moment and cannot be made universal practice.

value.zh: 周勃、霍光，其功至大，皆不聞有九錫之命也。」
value.en: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet never received the Nine Bestowals."
value.literal: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet one never hears of commands granting the Nine Bestowals."

value.zh: 張林積忿不已，以頌為張華之黨，將殺之。
value.en: Zhang Lin, still furious, treated Song as Zhang Hua's partisan and meant to kill him.
value.literal: Zhang Lin, nursing his wrath, took Song for a partisan of Zhang Hua and was about to kill him.

value.zh: 孫秀曰：「殺張、裴已傷時望，不可復殺頌。」
value.en: Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed public esteem. We cannot kill Song too."
value.literal: Sun Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed the age's esteem—we cannot kill Song again."

value.zh: 林乃止。
value.en: Lin desisted.
value.literal: Lin thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 以頌為光祿大夫。
value.en: Song was made Household Grandee.
value.literal: Song was made Household Grandee.

value.zh: 遂下詔加倫九錫，復加其子荂撫軍將軍，虔中軍將軍，詡為侍中。
value.en: An edict granted Lun the Nine Bestowals and further made Fu General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander, and Xu Attendant.
value.literal: An edict was then issued granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; his son Fu was further made General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander of the Army, and Xu Attendant.

value.zh: 又加孫秀侍中、輔國將軍，相國司馬、右率如故。
value.en: Xiu was made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.
value.literal: Sun Xiu was further made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.

value.zh: 張林等並居顯要。
value.en: Zhang Lin and others all held prominent posts.
value.literal: Zhang Lin and the rest all held prominent posts.

value.zh: 增相府兵為二萬人，與宿衛同，並所隱匿之兵，數逾三萬。
value.en: Chancellor household troops were raised to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard; with hidden forces the total exceeded thirty thousand.
value.literal: The chancellor's household troops were increased to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard, and with hidden troops as well the number exceeded thirty thousand.

value.zh: 倫及諸子皆頑鄙無識，秀狡黠貪淫，所與共事者，皆邪佞之士，惟競榮利，無深謀遠略，志趣乖異，互相憎嫉。
value.en: Lun and his sons were dull and vulgar; Xiu was cunning, greedy, and lewd. Their associates were corrupt men who sought only profit, without foresight, mutually hostile.
value.literal: Lun and his sons were all obtuse and vulgar without understanding; Xiu was cunning, greedy, and licentious; those who worked with them were all depraved men who competed only for glory and profit, without deep plans or far sight, their aims divergent and mutually hateful.

value.zh: 秀子會為射聲校尉，形貌短陋，如奴僕之下者，秀使尚帝女河東公主。
value.en: Xiu's son Hui, Colonel of the Archers, was short and ugly as a menial, yet Xiu married him to the Princess of Hedong.
value.literal: Xiu's son Hui was Colonel of the Archers; short and ugly in form, like one beneath a slave—yet Xiu had him marry the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Hedong.
